parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size, 1 to 1,000 (default 100).

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque cursor from the previous page's `next_cursor`.

parameters.name: at_least
parameters.description: Read at least this store revision (read-your-writes after a write).

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only addresses with one of these statuses: `planned`, `active`, `reserved` or `deprecated`. Repeat the parameter or separate the values with commas.

parameters.name: vrf
parameters.description: Only addresses of this VRF (identifier).

parameters.name: within
parameters.description: Only addresses inside this network, for example `192.0.2.0/24`. A bare address is a host network. Host bits must be zero.

parameters.name: prefix
parameters.description: Only addresses whose most specific prefix is this prefix (identifier).

parameters.name: interface
parameters.description: Only addresses assigned to this interface (identifier).

parameters.name: host
parameters.description: Only addresses assigned to an interface of this host (identifier).

parameters.name: tag
parameters.description: Only addresses that carry every one of these tags. Repeat the parameter or separate the tags with commas.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Case-insensitive text search over the address, the DNS name, the description and the tags.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sort order: comma-separated fields, `-` in front for descending, for example `-updated,ip`. Fields: `ip` (the default), `dns_name`, `status`, `created`, `updated`.

parameters.name: deleted
parameters.description: Deleted addresses: `exclude` (the default), `include` or `only` (the restore view).

parameters.name: expand
parameters.description: `host`: each address bound to an interface also carries `interface_detail` (`id`, `name`, `mac`, `duid`) and `host` (`id`, `name`, `mode`, `lock`), read from the same view as the page. Both are absent for an unbound address, when the interface or host is deleted, and when the principal may not read interfaces and hosts. Does not change the cursor.

200.description: A page of addresses

parameters.name: dry_run
parameters.description: Plan the change and return the plan without writing (API-09).

parameters.name: acknowledge
parameters.description:
Warning codes to acknowledge, comma-separated (for example
`ipam.prefix.nibble_boundary`).

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Repeating a POST with the same key returns the first result (API-04).

200.description: The plan of a dry run, or the first result again for a repeated `Idempotency-Key` (`replayed` is true)

409.description: The address exists in the VRF, no prefix contains it, it is a network or broadcast address, a DHCP pool covers it for a reserved host, the VRF or interface is missing, or the identifier is in use (`ipam.address.duplicate`, `ipam.address.no_prefix`, `ipam.address.network_or_broadcast`, `ipam.address.in_dhcp_pool`, `ipam.reference_missing`, `ipam.id_taken`)

422.description: The `Idempotency-Key` was used for a different request (`ipam.idempotency_mismatch`)

423.description: The host of the interface is locked against automation (`ipam.host.locked`)

post.description: Writes the IPAM rows a DHCP reservation is derived from (docs/dhcp.md section 2) in one batch: the host (`host`, or `new_host` for a new one, else the host of the address's interface) becomes `reserved`; the interface (`interface`, or `new_interface`, else the address's interface on that host, else the host's only interface, else a new `eth0`) gets `mac` and `client_id`; the address is bound to it with `status` `active` or `planned`. The address must lie in a prefix with a DHCP scope; the scope need not be enabled. Checked like the IPAM writes it makes; one audit record `ipam.address.reserve`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Address identifier

parameters.name: dry_run
parameters.description: Plan the change and return the plan without writing (API-09).

parameters.name: acknowledge
parameters.description:
Warning codes to acknowledge, comma-separated (for example
`ipam.prefix.nibble_boundary`).

200.description: The reservation's rows after the change, or the plan of a dry run

404.description: No such address (`ipam.not_found`), or its prefix has no DHCP scope (`dhcp.scope.not_found`)

409.description: Another reserved host holds the address or presents the client identity in the scope (`dhcp.reservation.conflict`, IPAM-23), the interface has no MAC address or client identifier (`dhcp.reservation.no_identity`, IPAM-18), the address lies in a DHCP pool (`ipam.address.in_dhcp_pool`), or another IPAM conflict (`ipam.name_taken`, `ipam.reference_missing`, `ipam.object_deleted`, `ipam.status.transition`, `ipam.plan.unacknowledged`)

412.description: An object changed between the read and the write (`ipam.revision_mismatch`)

423.description: The host is locked against automation (`ipam.host.locked`)

get.description: Newest first unless `order=asc`. Filters combine with AND. `principal` is a subject such as `user:<uuid>`, `token:<uuid>` or `system:api`; `action` is exact or, when it ends with a dot, a namespace prefix such as `ipam.prefix.`; `object` is a kind such as `prefix`, or `kind:uuid`. Records are read in sequence order and a request examines at most 20,000 of them: when that runs out first, the page holds the matches found so far, possibly none, and `next_cursor` continues the scan. `next_cursor` is null only when the scan reached the end of the log.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size, 1 to 1,000 (default 100).

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque cursor from the previous page's `next_cursor`.

parameters.name: at_least
parameters.description: Read at least this store revision (read-your-writes).

parameters.name: principal
parameters.description: Principal subject, for example `user:<uuid>`, `token:<uuid>` or `system:api`.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description:
Audit action, exact (`ipam.prefix.create`) or a namespace prefix ending with a dot
(`ipam.` or `ipam.prefix.`).

parameters.name: object
parameters.description: Object reference `kind:<uuid>`, or a bare kind such as `prefix`.

parameters.name: outcome
parameters.description: Outcome: `success`, `denied` or `failed`.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Records at or after this time (RFC 3339).

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Records before this time (RFC 3339).

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: `desc` (newest first, the default) or `asc`.

200.description: A page of audit records

get.summary: Read the audit log in sequence order for an export
get.description: Every record from `from` in sequence order with the anchor before it, for `tenko audit export`. Needs the global read permission on the audit log, as `GET /audit/verify`; a principal with scoped grants only is refused, because an export is only verifiable whole.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: The first sequence number (default 1).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Records per page, 1 to 5,000 (default 1,000).

200.description: A page of records

400.description: `from` or `limit` is out of range or malformed

get.summary: Verify the hash chain of the audit log
get.description: Walks the whole chain from record 1 and reports the first record that does not verify: a gap in the sequence, a record that does not link to its predecessor, or one whose hash no longer matches its content. `checked` counts the records that did verify, `head` is the last of them and `store_head` the newest record of the log. Reads the whole log; on a long log it takes a while.

200.description: The verification report; `intact` is false when the chain is broken

parameters.name: seq
parameters.description: Sequence number of the audit record, from 1

200.description: The audit record

400.description: The sequence number is not a positive integer

404.description: No record has this sequence number

Credential columns (login, password) are never IPAM fields: each host's login and
password become one operator secret of that host in the vault. Apply refuses them with
403 `import.credentials.vault_required` unless the server has a vault and the principal
passes both `Action::Create` and `Action::Reveal` on `ObjectKind::Secret` (in practice
an administrator with a password-or-stronger session, the IAM-07 threshold). The problem
carries the parameter `reason`, one of `vault_unavailable`, `step_up_required`,
`forbidden`, `unauthenticated` or `pin_coupling`, for a step-up `required`, the weakest
session strength that would do, and for `pin_coupling` `accounts`, the accounts that may
reveal but sign in with a PIN alone (the rule of `POST /secrets`). Setting `options.credentials` to `skip` in the mapping leaves the
credential columns out and the rest of the import is applied.

Credential columns (login, password) are never IPAM fields: each host's login and
password would become one operator secret of that host in the vault. `credentials`
says how many secrets would be created, replaced or left as they are, whether this
account may store them (`allowed`) and, when it may not, why (`reason`); then
`import.credentials.vault_required` is among the `blockers`. Storing them needs a vault
on the server and a principal that passes both create and reveal on secrets, in practice
an administrator with a password-or-stronger session (IAM-07), and no other account that
may reveal secrets signing in with a PIN alone (`reason` `pin_coupling`, as for
`POST /secrets`). Setting `options.credentials` to `skip` in the mapping leaves them out.

Expired but within the stale window: it answers only when the upstreams fail

busiest CPU, the smallest share of memory and of disk available.

the first reading and where the CPU is not read (Windows).

disk_total.description: The size of the file system of the data directory in bytes.

same ones and the cluster takes the highest count.

than the retention (default 900).
